headline.headline: TIGERS SHUT OUT RANGERS, 3-0, BEHIND GREENE'S 12th BLAST
headline.deck: Detroit silences Texas from the first pitch, Greene's homer headlines a complete effort.
headline.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas — The Detroit Tigers needed all nine innings of holiday baseball to prove their point, and they made it decisively, blanking the Texas Rangers 3-0 on Saturday at Globe Life Field behind a crisp, efficient performance that left 37,576 fans heading home early on the Fourth of July weekend.

Riley Greene provided the lasting image, launching his 12th home run of the season to stake Detroit to an early lead it would never relinquish. The Tigers scored twice in the first inning and added an insurance run in the second, then handed the ball to starter Chris Martin, who locked down the Rangers the rest of the way. Martin earned the win while the Detroit defense backed him without incident across the final seven shutout frames.

The complete-game effort took just 2 hours and 22 minutes, one of the quickest finishes of any game on the Independence Day weekend slate. Josh Jung doubled for one of the few Texas bright spots, but the Rangers never mustered a sustained threat against a Detroit pitching staff that looked sharp from the opening pitch. Dillon Dingler was hit by a pitch from Cal Quantrill in the game, with Texas's Shane Carter also taking one from Jack Flaherty in what was otherwise a clean, professional Tigers victory.

secondary.headline: MARINERS ROLL BLUE JAYS 11-0 IN SEATTLE ROUT
secondary.deck: Seattle pours on five runs in the second inning and never looks back against Toronto.
secondary.body:
SEATTLE — The Seattle Mariners turned Safeco Field into a holiday showcase, dismantling the Toronto Blue Jays 11-0 before 41,181 fans on Saturday. The damage came in waves: five runs in the second inning set the tone, and Seattle added two more in the fifth before erupting for four in the sixth to put the game well out of reach.

Toronto managed nothing across all nine frames, with starter Steve Macko hitting Luke Raley during the game but doing little else to affect the outcome. The Blue Jays were blanked by a Seattle staff that yielded zero baserunners of consequence throughout the afternoon. The shutout pushed the Mariners' confidence heading into the holiday weekend, while Toronto's struggles on the road continued in embarrassing fashion.

secondary.headline: PREDATORS LOCK UP BOURQUE ON SIX-YEAR DEAL AS FREE AGENCY HEATS UP
secondary.deck: Nashville commits $33 million to 24-year-old center Mavrik Bourque, three days after acquiring him.
secondary.body:
NASHVILLE — The Nashville Predators moved quickly to secure their newest piece, signing center Mavrik Bourque to a six-year, $33 million contract Saturday, just three days after acquiring the 24-year-old. The deal signals Nashville's commitment to building around younger talent as the organization looks toward a competitive future following this spring's playoff run.

Bourque, a skilled center with upside at his age, gives the Predators a cornerstone piece at a position of need. The signing came as NHL free agency continued to reshape rosters across the league, with Detroit also adding forward Chase Stillman on a one-year deal Saturday. For Nashville general manager Barry Trotz, locking up Bourque long-term before another team could make a run at him was a clear organizational priority.

secondary.headline: PETERSON ERUPTS FOR 28 IN SUMMER LEAGUE DEBUT, BOOZER ADDS 15
secondary.deck: Two of the draft class's top prospects make strong first impressions in Las Vegas.
secondary.body:
LAS VEGAS — The next generation of NBA talent put on a show Saturday, as Darryn Peterson and Cameron Boozer turned in commanding summer league debuts. Peterson led the way with 28 points, showcasing the scoring versatility that made him one of the draft's most coveted prospects, while Boozer chipped in 15 in a performance that reinforced his reputation as a polished young forward.

Both players arrived carrying significant expectations, and neither shrank from them on the Las Vegas floor. For front offices still monitoring the summer league as a final evaluation tool, Peterson's burst of offensive production was the most attention-grabbing performance of the weekend. Boozer, the son of former NBA forward Carlos Boozer, showed a composure and feel for the game that suggested he would not need an extended adjustment period at the professional level.

column.headline: DETROIT'S QUIET FOURTH IS ACTUALLY THE LOUDEST STATEMENT IN BASEBALL
column.body:
While most of the country was watching fireworks and grilling in the backyard, the Detroit Tigers went to Arlington and delivered a message that deserves more than a box score glance. A 3-0 shutout on the road, finished in under two and a half hours, with Riley Greene doing Greene things and the pitching staff doing the rest — that is a team that knows exactly who it is heading into the second half of the season.

The Rangers, playing at home in front of more than 37,000 fans, never had a real answer. That is not a fluke. Detroit has been one of the quieter success stories of 2026, building wins the old-fashioned way, and Saturday afternoon in Texas was the clearest evidence yet that this club is worth watching closely as the calendar turns toward August. The Tigers did not need the drama. They just needed the win, and they got it with room to spare.

story.headline: TWINS POUND SEVEN HOME RUNS, ROUT YANKEES 11-4 ON INDEPENDENCE DAY
story.deck: Minnesota explodes for historic Bronx blowout, stranding 22 Yankees on base
story.body:
NEW YORK — The Minnesota Twins turned the Fourth of July into their own personal fireworks show at Yankee Stadium, clubbing seven home runs in an 11-4 demolition of New York on Saturday before a crowd of 40,156. The Twins wasted no time, scoring five runs across the first two innings and never looking back, while a Yankees lineup that put 22 runners on base could not deliver when it counted.

Larnach, Clemens, Bell, Keaschall, Jackson, Dominguez and Schuemann all went deep for Minnesota, a power display that overwhelmed a Yankees pitching staff already in disarray. Bell and Dominguez each added doubles, and Byron Buxton contributed a two-bagger as the Twins finished with 14 runners left on base of their own while still manufacturing runs with relentless efficiency. A four-run eighth inning salted the game away after New York had briefly trimmed the deficit with a three-run fifth.

The loss was a gut punch for New York, whose 22 stranded baserunners told the story of a lineup unable to convert opportunity into runs against Minnesota's pitching. Keaschall was hit by a pitch from Bird, and Rice was plunked by Ta Rogers, but neither disruption slowed the Twins' march. Minnesota's early and late burst framed a commanding road victory that underscored the gap between these two American League clubs at the midpoint of the 2026 season.

story.headline: EWING RETURNS TO THE SIDELINE, JOINING WIZARDS STAFF AS KEEFE'S ASSISTANT
story.deck: Georgetown and Knicks legend brings Hall of Fame pedigree to rebuilding Washington franchise.
story.body:
Patrick Ewing, the Hall of Fame center whose imposing presence defined Georgetown basketball and a generation of New York Knicks basketball, has agreed to join head coach Brian Keefe's staff in Washington as an assistant coach, sources confirmed Sunday. The move reunites Ewing with the NBA sideline and gives the rebuilding Wizards a marquee name whose knowledge of big-man development could prove invaluable as Washington attempts to reshape its frontcourt identity.

Ewing, 63, brings decades of playing and coaching experience to the role. He served as head coach at Georgetown from 2017 through 2025, compiling a modest record but earning widespread respect for his player development work with young centers and power forwards. His presence on Keefe's bench signals the Wizards' intention to accelerate the growth of their frontcourt prospects, a priority for a franchise that has struggled to find its footing since trading away veteran cornerstones in recent rebuilding moves.

The hiring arrives as Washington's front office monitors a busy free agency landscape, with the broader NBA humming over LeBron James's next destination and veteran center Andre Drummond drawing fresh attention after agreeing to terms with the New York Knicks. Meanwhile, the summer league in Las Vegas produced two electric debuts, with rookie Darryn Peterson scorching nets for 28 points and fellow first-year player Cameron Boozer adding 15, injecting optimism into franchises hungry for young talent to build around.

story.headline: FLYERS MAKE BOLD PLAY FOR DUCKS STAR CARLSSON WITH OFFER SHEET
story.deck: Philadelphia targets Anaheim's elite center as NHL's summer spending spree hits high gear.
story.body:
The Philadelphia Flyers fired the most explosive shot of the 2026 NHL free agency period Friday, tendering an offer sheet to Anaheim Ducks star center Leo Carlsson on a five-year deal, daring the rebuilding Ducks to match the commitment or surrender one of the game's brightest young pivots. Carlsson, 21, emerged as one of the most dangerous two-way centers in the Western Conference last season, and the Flyers' front office made clear that Philadelphia intends to compete for a playoff spot sooner rather than later. The Ducks have a limited window to match the offer sheet or receive compensatory draft picks in return.

The Carlsson drama headlined a busy Saturday across the league, with the Nashville Predators locking up newly acquired center Mavrik Bourque on a six-year, $33 million contract just three days after acquiring the 24-year-old. The deal signals Nashville's commitment to rebuilding its forward core around young talent after a turbulent stretch of seasons. Bourque, a shifty and defensively responsible pivot, is expected to slot into a top-six role immediately for a Predators club hungry to return to playoff relevance in the Central Division.

Elsewhere, the Toronto Maple Leafs wasted no time securing the future, signing No. 1 overall pick Gavin McKenna to a three-year entry-level contract, while forward Chase Stillman, the St. Louis native and former New Jersey Devils first-round pick from 2021, agreed to a one-year deal with the Detroit Red Wings. McKenna's signing drew immediate fanfare in Toronto, where expectations for the phenom are already soaring ahead of his first NHL training camp.

story.headline: QUARTERBACKS ON THE MOVE AS NFL OFFSEASON RESHAPES THE LEAGUE
story.deck: Several teams overhauled their rosters this spring in pursuit of a franchise passer.
story.body:
The quarterback carousel that has defined the 2026 NFL offseason showed no signs of slowing down this week, with multiple franchises finalizing deals that will reshape their rosters heading into training camp. The Las Vegas Raiders locked up veteran signal-caller Sam Darnold on a three-year contract worth $112 million, betting the former Minnesota standout can stabilize a position that has been in flux in the Nevada desert for years. Meanwhile, the Cleveland Browns completed a stunning trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers, acquiring Russell Wilson in exchange for a package of draft picks that includes a first-rounder in 2027.

The 2026 NFL Draft, held in Green Bay last month, added fresh fuel to the fire. Quarterback Shedeur Sanders, selected fourth overall by the New Orleans Saints, has already begun private workouts with new offensive coordinator Kliff Kingsbury, a pairing that has generated considerable buzz around the league. The Carolina Panthers, holding the top pick, surprised observers by taking Colorado wide receiver Travis Hunter, signaling confidence in incumbent starter Bryce Young heading into his make-or-break third season.

On the defensive side of the ball, the Dallas Cowboys made the splashiest move of the spring by signing pass rusher Micah Parsons to a massive extension, keeping the four-time Pro Bowl selection off the open market through the 2030 season. General manager Jerry Jones called it the most important signing in franchise history since Dak Prescott. Training camps open across the league in late July, and coaches from San Francisco to Philadelphia are warning that this offseason's aggressive roster construction means preseason battles will be fiercer than ever.
